M&P® M2.0® POLYMER-FRAME PISTOLS — p/n 3006363  REV:M&P_M2.0_POLYMER_FRAME_021525 (2025)
cleanIntro: Smith & Wesson's M&P M2.0 polymer-frame pistol manual covers the M&P9 M2.0 Full, and its takedown is the one that needs no trigger pull: the frame tool drops the sear deactivation lever and the takedown lever rotates. Every step below carries the manual's words and the page they are on.

steps.title: Make sure this is the book for your pistol, and what is fitted to it
steps.action: This procedure comes from Smith & Wesson's manual for M&P M2.0 polymer-frame pistols, and the M&P9 M2.0 Full is one. Two neighbours are handed away on the same cover line and are NOT covered here: the original series M&P polymer-frame pistols go to a separate manual, #441300000, and M&P metal-frame pistols go to a separate manual, #3014737. Then work out what is actually on your gun — a manual thumb safety or not, and which of the two loaded chamber indicators it carries.
steps.prose: The book never prints "M&P9 M2.0 Full" as such; it scopes itself to M2.0 polymer-frame pistols and then treats size, caliber and features as options within that. Full-size and compact M2.0 pistols share this takedown exactly; the full-size simply carries the longer barrel, slide and grip. That is why the warning below is in capitals: several sections of this manual apply only if your pistol is so equipped, and the book will not tell you which ones — you have to look.
steps.aside: The original series M&P® polymer frame pistols are covered in a separate manual (#441300000). M&P® metal frame pistols are covered in a separate manual (#3014737).
steps.quote: YOU MUST DETERMINE WHICH FEATURES ARE PRESENT ON YOUR SPECIFIC M&P® M2.0® PISTOL AND HOW THOSE FEATURES OPERATE.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
M&P® M2.0® POLYMER-FRAME PISTOLS — p/n 3006363  REV:M&P_M2.0_POLYMER_FRAME_021525 — Model & Features Identification, p.12

steps.title: Magazine out, slide back, chamber cleared
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction with your finger off the trigger and outside the trigger guard. Depress the magazine release and remove the magazine, then grasp the serrated sides of the slide from the rear and briskly draw it fully rearward to extract any cartridge from the chamber and throw it clear.
steps.prose: Brisk is the operative word: easing the slide back lets an extracted round tumble in the ejection port instead of leaving, and a round that comes to rest on the feed ramp can be fed straight back into the chamber when the slide runs home. Do not put a hand or a finger over the ejection port while you do it.
steps.quote: briskly draw the slide fully rearward in order to extract any cartridge from the barrel chamber and clear it from the pistol.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
M&P® M2.0® POLYMER-FRAME PISTOLS — p/n 3006363  REV:M&P_M2.0_POLYMER_FRAME_021525 — Unloading, p.25

steps.title: Lock the slide open and look twice
steps.action: Let the slide move slightly forward from its rearmost position while pressing upward on the slide stop, so the slide locks open. Then look into the chamber and down through the magazine well, and satisfy yourself no ammunition remains in the pistol.
steps.prose: Two windows, two separate facts. The chamber tells you the barrel is empty; the magazine well tells you nothing is left to feed it. Unload the magazine itself as well, pressing each cartridge forward and out with the bullet end pointed away from you.
steps.quote: Look into the chamber and down through the magazine well. Verify that no ammunition remains in the pistol
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
M&P® M2.0® POLYMER-FRAME PISTOLS — p/n 3006363  REV:M&P_M2.0_POLYMER_FRAME_021525 — Unloading, p.25
steps.warn: The marking table in this manual lists 9mm Luger as OK for standard and OK for +P, and NO for +P+.

steps.title: Frame tool out of the grip, palmswell insert off
steps.action: With the slide locked open and the pistol confirmed empty, take the frame tool out of the bottom of the grip by turning it 90 degrees in either direction and pulling it free. Then tip the interchangeable palmswell backstrap insert away from the frame, bottom first, to release the tab at the top.
steps.prose: The frame tool lives in the grip precisely so it is with the pistol when you need it — it is the same tool used to change palmswells and it is the one this takedown calls for. Take the insert off bottom-first: prising from the top loads the tab in the direction it is designed to resist and is how they crack.
steps.quote: Remove the frame tool from the bottom of the grip by turning it 90 degrees (in either direction) and pulling it out of the frame
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
M&P® M2.0® POLYMER-FRAME PISTOLS — p/n 3006363  REV:M&P_M2.0_POLYMER_FRAME_021525 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.27

steps.title: Push the sear deactivation lever down
steps.action: Using the frame tool, reach down through the opening left by the palmswell insert and push the sear deactivation lever down into the lowered position. It is coloured yellow or green so you can see it.
steps.prose: This is what makes the M2.0 takedown a no-trigger-pull takedown, and it is the whole safety argument for this design: the lever holds the sear out of the way so the pistol comes apart without anyone ever having to point it somewhere and press the trigger. If it will not go down, do not force it and do not fall back on pulling the trigger — check the slide is genuinely locked open first.
steps.caution: The sear deactivation lever is yellow/green in color.
steps.quote: Use the frame tool provided (or a similar device) to push the sear deactivation lever down into the lowered position
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
M&P® M2.0® POLYMER-FRAME PISTOLS — p/n 3006363  REV:M&P_M2.0_POLYMER_FRAME_021525 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.27

steps.title: Rotate the takedown lever clockwise
steps.action: Rotate the takedown lever clockwise until it stops.
steps.prose: The lever sits on the left of the frame above the trigger and swings down to a vertical position. It will only rotate with the slide locked back, because that is what aligns the barrel lug clear of it — if it feels solid, the slide has crept forward off the slide stop.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
M&P® M2.0® POLYMER-FRAME PISTOLS — p/n 3006363  REV:M&P_M2.0_POLYMER_FRAME_021525 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.27

steps.title: Slide off the frame, controlling the recoil spring
steps.action: Grasp the slide from the top, ease it slightly rearward to release it from the slide stop, then run it forward off the front of the frame — keeping hold of the recoil spring and guide rod assembly the whole time.
steps.prose: The recoil spring is compressed as the slide comes off the rails and it is captive only as far as the guide rod holds it. Let go at that moment and the spring assembly leaves the pistol under its own power. Keep the muzzle end pointed away from your face throughout.
steps.quote: remove the slide from the frame by pulling it slightly rearward then forward while being careful to retain the recoil spring and guide rod assembly
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
M&P® M2.0® POLYMER-FRAME PISTOLS — p/n 3006363  REV:M&P_M2.0_POLYMER_FRAME_021525 — Field Stripping / Disassembly, p.28
steps.warn: YOU MUST CONTROL THE SLIDE AND THE RECOIL SPRING DURING REMOVAL TO KEEP THEM FROM FLYING OFF AND CAUSING INJURY.

steps.title: Recoil spring out, then the barrel
steps.action: Lift the recoil spring and guide rod assembly out from below the barrel, then take the barrel out of the bottom of the slide.
steps.prose: The spring assembly unseats from its recess in the barrel lug at the rear and its housing at the muzzle end, so it comes out with a slight compression rather than a pull. Once it is clear the barrel tips out of the bottom of the slide with nothing holding it.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil spring from below the barrel
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
M&P® M2.0® POLYMER-FRAME PISTOLS — p/n 3006363  REV:M&P_M2.0_POLYMER_FRAME_021525 — Field Stripping / Disassembly, p.28

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Slide, barrel, recoil spring assembly, frame, palmswell insert, frame tool and magazine. That is the whole strip Smith & Wesson publishes for this pistol, and it reaches everything the cleaning below asks for.
steps.prose: The manual draws its line here in capitals and repeats it in the assembly section. The striker, the sear housing and the fire control parts stay in the pistol; anything past this point needs a qualified gunsmith and factory-authorized parts.
steps.quote: NEVER DISASSEMBLE YOUR FIREARM BEYOND THE DISASSEMBLY/FIELD STRIPPING PROCEDURE DETAILED IN THIS MANUAL
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
M&P® M2.0® POLYMER-FRAME PISTOLS — p/n 3006363  REV:M&P_M2.0_POLYMER_FRAME_021525 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.26

deepAbsentReason: The M&P M2.0 polymer-frame manual documents inspecting, the manual thumb safety, the loaded chamber indicators, loading, firing, misfeeds, unloading, field stripping, lubrication, assembly, palmswell inserts, the reversible magazine release, the magazine, rear sight adjustment, cleaning and maintenance, the C.O.R.E. optical sight adapter and the over-travel adjustment screw — and no disassembly past the field strip. It prints the boundary in capitals in both the field-stripping and assembly sections, and it documents no magazine disassembly at all. Searched and re-confirmed against the cached document on 2026-08-20: Smith & Wesson publishes no deeper procedure for the M&P9 M2.0 Full. Basic clean as set out above covers routine care; deeper work is gunsmith territory.

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHAMBER
tasks: Remove excessive firing residue from the bore and chamber with a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent — a 9mm brush and jag, not whatever is in the kit
Finish by running a dry cotton cloth patch through the bore and chamber to carry residue and solvent out
Clean the outside of the barrel, the hood, the locking lug and the feed ramp; the ramp is where a feeding problem usually starts

cleaning.name: SLIDE AND FRAME
tasks: Clean the breech face, under and around the extractor claw, and the striker channel opening
Clean the slide rails and the frame rails, and wipe the recoil spring and guide rod down rather than soaking them
Clean out the magazine well and the frame interior, taking care not to dislodge the sear deactivation lever
Clean the exterior with a non-abrasive cloth and remove every trace of cleaning solution, oil and fingerprints

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION — EIGHT POINTS, ONE DROP EACH
tasks: Smith & Wesson names eight lubrication points and asks for a single drop of high-quality firearms lubricant at each
Do not over-lubricate: excess oil collects unburned powder and carbon and that residue can interfere with proper functioning
Wipe the excess off after lubricating and leave a film, not a pool

cleaning.name: IF YOUR PISTOL IS SO EQUIPPED
tasks: Ported barrel: never install a ported barrel in a pistol with a non-ported slide, and keep the ports clear of fouling
C.O.R.E. optical sight adapter: those instructions apply only to M&P M2.0 C.O.R.E. pistols — do not work a plate or screw matrix onto a slide that is not cut for one
Manual thumb safety: wipe around the lever and confirm it still moves fully up to SAFE and fully down to FIRE after cleaning

cleaning.name: AVOID, AND BEFORE STORAGE
tasks: Avoid prolonged solvent immersion and prolonged ultrasonic cleaning; never use ammoniated or other strong alkaline solvents
For extended storage oil the bore, chamber and internal surfaces and coat the external metal with an anti-rust oil
Do not store the pistol in leather or heavy cloth, or with a plug in the barrel
Check for signs of wear every time you clean it; if wear is noted, stop using the pistol

reassembly: Replace the barrel in the slide so the muzzle is flush with the end of the slide and the barrel lug is turned up away from the ejection port.

Put the smaller protruding end of the recoil spring guide assembly into the slide guide housing at the muzzle, seat the rear of the assembly in the recess on the barrel lug, and check it is centred and seated rather than sitting alongside.
Confirm the sear deactivation lever is still in the lowered position, protruding into the magazine well, and that the slide stop is down.

With the takedown lever down, put the rear of the slide onto the front frame rails and pull it back onto the rear rails, then rotate the takedown lever back up, refit the palmswell insert and stow the frame tool in the grip.
fncheck: With the magazine out and the chamber visually confirmed empty: rack the slide several times and check it runs fully into battery each time. Confirm the slide stop holds the slide open when pressed up with the slide back, and drops it cleanly. Check the takedown lever is fully returned to its up position — a lever left partly rotated will let the slide come off under recoil. If a manual thumb safety is fitted, confirm it blocks the trigger fully in SAFE and releases it in FIRE. Seat an empty magazine, pull on it to confirm the catch holds, then press the release and check it drops free.
